answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils with aging-weighted reputation: every identity starts on a small knoll of zero trust and gains weight only through weeks of peer-verified, useful work, like a lotus that earns its bloom slowly. Influence and payouts scale with that aged history and decay during idleness, so a fresh identity cannot vote or earn. An attacker spinning up a nebula of thousands of fake agents would have to fund real work for each one, for weeks, before any of them matter - the cost of the farm exceeds the reward it could steal.
